summary: Romania has been a full Schengen member since January 2025: EU citizens enter freely, visa-exempt nationalities such as the US and UK get 90 days in any 180-day period counted together with the rest of the Schengen Area, and other passports need a Schengen visa applied for via Romania's official eVisa portal. The currency remains the leu, not the euro.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

source.name: European Commission — Schengen short-stay calculator (DG Migration and Home Affairs)

fee.notes: Children 6–11: €45; under 6: free. Fee set EU-wide since June 11, 2024. Applications start on the official eVisa portal and are decided by the Romanian consulate serving your residence.

source.name: eVisa Romania — Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa portal

fee.notes: For stays over 90 days — work, study, family reunification and other long-stay purposes; converted into a residence permit after arrival. Confirm the current fee for your category with the consulate.

source.name: eVisa Romania — Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa portal

passportValidity.text: Non-EU passports must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen Area and have been issued within the last 10 years. EU/EEA citizens only need a valid passport or national ID card.

source.name: eVisa Romania — Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa portal
eVisa Romania — Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa portal

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it but border officers may ask about cover.

source.name: eVisa Romania — Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa portal

onwardTicket.text: Border officers may ask non-EU visitors for proof of return or onward travel and accommodation details.

source.name: eVisa Romania — Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa portal

proofOfFunds.text: Romania's guideline for short-stay visa applicants is €50 per day (minimum €500 for the whole stay). Visa-exempt visitors are rarely asked but should be able to show means of support. Confirm current amounts with the consulate.

source.name: eVisa Romania — Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa portal

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border. There is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorization System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is being phased in. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

notes: No limits on goods for personal use when arriving from another EU country.
Duty-free from outside the EU: 200 cigarettes, 1 liter of spirits, goods up to €300 (€430 arriving by air/sea).

payments.text: Cards and contactless are standard in cities, supermarkets and chain restaurants, but keep some lei for markets, small-town shops, rural guesthouses and some taxis.

safety.text: Romania is one of the EU's safer destinations with low violent crime. Watch for pickpocketing on public transport in Bucharest, taxi overcharging around stations and the airport, and stray dogs in some areas.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Romania Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: May–September is best for Transylvania's towns, Carpathian hiking and the Black Sea coast; late spring and September avoid the summer heat in Bucharest.

roadVignette.appliesTo: Category A — cars and light vehicles up to 3.5 t — on the national road network, motorways included.
roadVignette.text: The rovinieta covers Romania's national roads, not only its motorways, and is registered to the number plate. Tariffs are set in euro and charged in lei at the official rate (5.2439 RON/EUR at the time of checking). The Fetești–Cernavodă bridge on the A2 toward the coast is tolled on top of the rovinieta — 19 RON per crossing for a car.

driving.text: Romania is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Romania yet.

tips.text: Romania is in the EU and Schengen but not the eurozone. Pay in Romanian lei (RON); places quoting euros to tourists usually apply poor exchange rates.

Since January 2025 Romania is a full Schengen member: no more checks at the land borders with Hungary and Bulgaria, and days spent in Romania count toward the same 90-in-180 allowance as France or Germany.
In Bucharest use ride-hailing apps (Bolt, Uber) or order taxis through an app — overcharging of tourists at the airport and Gara de Nord is a long-running problem.
The Carpathians hold Europe's largest brown-bear population — never feed or approach bears, keep food sealed when camping, and heed local warnings on hiking routes.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Romania?
faq.answer: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens don't need a visa. Citizens of the Schengen visa-waiver countries — including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan — can stay 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa. Other nationalities need a Schengen short-stay visa, applied for through Romania's official eVisa portal (evisa.mae.ro) and the consulate serving their residence.

faq.question: Is Romania in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: Yes. Romania joined Schengen for air and sea borders in March 2024 and became a full member — land borders included — on January 1, 2025. A Romanian-issued Schengen visa is valid for the whole area, and vice versa.

faq.question: Does Romania use the euro?
faq.answer: No. The currency is the Romanian leu (RON). Cards are widely accepted in cities, and euros are best exchanged at banks or reputable exchange offices rather than spent directly.

faq.question: Do days in Romania count toward the Schengen 90/180 limit?
faq.answer: Yes, since full Schengen membership in 2025 — time spent in Romania is counted together with days in all other Schengen countries. Before 2024 Romania had a separate 90-day allowance; that is no longer the case.

faq.question: Can Moldovan citizens travel to Romania visa-free?
faq.answer: Yes — Moldovan citizens with a biometric passport can enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU's visa-free regime; many Moldovans also hold Romanian (EU) citizenship, which gives full freedom of movement.
